name: merge.zoo
title: Merge Two or More zoo Objects

origin.description: Align zoo series on a shared index.
origin.usage: merge.zoo(..., all = TRUE, fill = NA, suffixes = NULL, check.names = FALSE, retclass = c("zoo", "list", "data.frame"), drop = TRUE, sep = ".")

arguments.text: Series to align. The first is a zoo series. A plain vector with the same number of rows, or a length-one value, is placed on the first series' index.

arguments.name: all
arguments.text: Logical vector recycled to the number of series. TRUE keeps that series' index. FALSE keeps only indexes present in every series.

arguments.name: fill
arguments.text: Value written into gaps. The default is NA.

arguments.name: suffixes
arguments.text: Names used to build column names. When omitted, the call expressions are deparsed.

arguments.name: check.names
arguments.text: When TRUE, column names are made unique and syntactic.

arguments.name: retclass
arguments.text: "zoo" returns one series. "list" and "data.frame" return the aligned pieces. NULL updates each variable in the caller and returns NULL.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: When TRUE, a single remaining vector stays a vector. When FALSE, it stays a one-column matrix.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: Separator pasted between a suffix and a column name.

origin.details: The default result index is the union. all = FALSE is the intersection, and a mixed logical vector is a left or right join. A length-one plain value is stored on the first series' index, so a time that belongs only to a later series is still the fill. Duplicate indexes inside one series are an error.
origin.value: One zoo series, a list or data frame of aligned series, or NULL when retclass is NULL.
origin.example:
x <- zoo(c(1, 3, 5), c(1, 2, 4))
y <- zoo(c(2, 4, 6), c(2, 3, 4))
z <- merge(x, y)
show <- function(v) paste(vapply(as.numeric(v), function(a) if (is.na(a)) "NA" else sprintf("%.16g", a), ""), collapse = " ")
cat(show(coredata(z)), "\n", sep = "")
cat(show(index(z)), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Align zoo series on a shared index.
translation.usage: merge_zoo(*args, all=True, fill=nan, suffixes=None, check_names=False, retclass="zoo", drop=True, sep=".")

arguments.name: *args
arguments.text: Zoo series. A plain vector with the same number of rows, or a length-one number, is placed on the first series' index.

arguments.name: all
arguments.text: Logical vector recycled to the number of series. True keeps that series' index. False keeps only indexes present in every series.

arguments.name: fill
arguments.text: Value written into gaps. The default is NaN.

arguments.name: suffixes
arguments.text: Names used to build column names. When omitted, the names are X1, X2, and so on.

arguments.name: check_names
arguments.text: When True, column names are made unique and syntactic.

arguments.name: retclass
arguments.text: "zoo" returns one series. "list" returns a dict of aligned series. "data.frame" returns the index and the columns. None writes the aligned data back onto each Zoo and returns None.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: When True, a single remaining vector stays one-dimensional. When False, it stays a one-column matrix.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: Separator pasted between a suffix and a column name.

translation.details: The default result index is the union. all=False is the intersection, and a mixed logical vector is a left or right join. A length-one plain value is stored on the first series' index. Matrices are Fortran order. Column names follow the installed rules, including the last-suffix name used for an unnamed matrix when another series already has names.
translation.value: A Zoo, a dict of Zoo series, a dict of columns, or None when retclass is None.
translation.example:
import math
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.merge import merge_zoo

def show(values):
    array = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    flat = array.reshape(-1, order="F") if array.ndim == 2 else array.reshape(-1)
    parts = []
    for value in flat:
        value = float(value)
        parts.append("NA" if math.isnan(value) else format(value, ".16g"))
    return " ".join(parts)

x = Zoo([1.0, 3.0, 5.0], [1.0, 2.0, 4.0])
y = Zoo([2.0, 4.0, 6.0], [2.0, 3.0, 4.0])
z = merge_zoo(x, y)
print(show(z.data))
print(show(z.index))
